title: New Potato Salad with Chive
subtitle: Tender new potatoes in a light creme fraiche and chive dressing
excerpt: Small new potatoes dressed while warm in creme fraiche loosened with a touch of vinegar and plenty of fresh chives. A cleaner, lighter potato salad than the mayo-heavy version, and excellent with cold salmon.
sourceNotes: New potato salad with cream or creme fraiche is a feature of British summer cooking, particularly alongside cold poached salmon at garden parties. The combination of new potatoes, creme fraiche and chives has been recorded in British cookbooks from the 1970s onward, and reflects French influence on British dairy-based salad dressings.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best dressed and served the same day. Cook and cool the potatoes up to 4 hours ahead.

content.text: New potato salad with creme fraiche is the lighter summer alternative to the mayonnaise version. The key is dressing the potatoes while they are still warm, which helps the creme fraiche cling and the flavour absorb. Use good waxy new potatoes, cook them in well-salted water, and the rest takes less than five minutes.

Put the potatoes in a pan of cold, well-salted water. Bring to the boil and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, until a knife slides through without resistance. Drain and leave for 5 minutes, then halve any larger ones.

While the potatoes are still warm, stir together {{creme-fraiche}} of creme fraiche, {{cider-vinegar}} of cider vinegar, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Pour the dressing over the warm potatoes and toss gently to coat. Scatter over the chives and spring onion. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.cause: Potatoes were too cold when dressed.
items.fix: Dress the potatoes while they are still warm: the surface absorbs moisture from the dressing rather than repelling it.

items.cause: Potatoes undercooked or salting skipped in the water.
items.fix: Use well-salted water (as salty as light pasta water) and cook until completely tender. Under-seasoned potatoes at the cooking stage cannot be rescued with dressing alone.

content.text: New potato salad with creme fraiche appears at every British summer gathering where cold salmon is on the table. It is the lighter, sharper counterpart to the mayo version, and keeps well enough to sit on a buffet for a couple of hours without turning heavy. It travels well to picnics and works alongside any cold meat, smoked fish or grilled vegetable.
